section_summary: This section documents U.S. debates over restricting exports to Japan, especially aviation gasoline, petroleum technology, aircraft-grade alloys, lead, molybdenum, steel, and other strategic materials. It combines public petitions against aiding Japanese aggression in China with corporate requests for guidance and State Department efforts to administer a voluntary “moral embargo.” The section also records congressional inquiries, diplomatic reporting, and disputes over existing contracts between American companies and Japanese industrial concerns.

subfiles.title: White House referral to the State Department
subfiles.about: Refers correspondence concerning Japan-related trade policy to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: White House referral slip signed by Watson sending an unspecified communication to State.

subfiles.title: Senator Murray forwards Wong Sun's letter
subfiles.about: Forwards a constituent's appeal to President Roosevelt and requests confirmation of its receipt.
subfiles.summary: Senator Murray forwards a constituent Wong Sun's letter to the President and asks General Watson to acknowledge receipt.

subfiles.title: Wong Sun appeal against war-supply sales to Japan
subfiles.about: Asks the President to prevent sales of war supplies to Japan and avoid trade arrangements harmful to China.
subfiles.summary: Wong Sun condemns Japanese attacks on Chinese civilians and asks Roosevelt to stop war-supply sales and oppose a trade treaty with Japan harmful to China.

subfiles.title: State Department acknowledgment to Senator Murray
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Murray's transmittal of Wong Sun's letter concerning war supplies to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges the referral of Murray's letter and Wong Sun's appeal, noting new legislation would be required for the requested restrictions.

subfiles.title: White House referral of Washington Committee correspondence
subfiles.about: Refers a communication to State Department officials for attention and consideration.
subfiles.summary: White House referral, signed by Watson, of Washington Committee correspondence to State, routed to Hornbeck.

subfiles.title: Washington Committee for Aid to China policy appeal
subfiles.from: Mortimer Graves, Washington Committee for Aid to China
subfiles.about: Urges stronger American action against Japanese aggression and American exports supporting it.
subfiles.summary: Washington Committee for Aid to China urges nonrecognition of the Wang Ching-wei regime, postponing a new commercial treaty, ending war-material shipments, and a major loan to Chinese Industrial Cooperatives.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mortimer Graves
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the committee's letter on Far Eastern policy.
subfiles.summary: Department acknowledges Mortimer Graves's communication via the White House, saying the committee's views are carefully noted.
keywords: Washington Committee for Aid to China

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on molybdenum producers' export restraint
subfiles.from: Great Britain despatch attributed to Johnson
subfiles.about: References information that American molybdenum producers agreed temporarily not to export to Russia or Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Butterworth tells the Paris Embassy American producers agreed to suspend molybdenum exports to Russia and Japan.

subfiles.title: Senate forwarding memorandum concerning Samuel Wilson
subfiles.about: Forwards a constituent's inquiry for consideration and requests return of the letter.
subfiles.summary: Senator Davis forwards a communication on Samuel Wilson to the chief of Far Eastern Affairs, asking that it be handled and the original returned.

subfiles.title: Samuel Wilson inquiry about Japanese scrap buyers
subfiles.about: Seeks contacts with Japanese Government fiscal agents for clients wishing to sell scrap.
subfiles.summary: Samuel Wilson says junk-business clients want a direct link to Japanese Government fiscal agents, noting heavy San Francisco shipments and several carloads available.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Davis on Japanese fiscal agents
subfiles.about: Reports that the Department has no record of Japanese fiscal agents purchasing the requested material in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Department tells Senator Davis it knows of no Japanese Government fiscal agents in the country for such purchasing and returns Wilson's letter.

subfiles.title: Ethyl Gasoline Corporation report on tetraethyl lead shipments
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, attention Charles W. Yost
subfiles.about: Reports the quantity of British-associated ethyl fluid and tetraethyl lead shipped to Japan in 1939.
subfiles.summary: Ethyl Gasoline reports Associated Ethyl shipped 1,106,490 pounds of ethyl fluid, with 679,500 pounds of tetraethyl lead, to Japan from May to December 1939, none in 1940, and promises monthly reports.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Associated Ethyl shipment report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the report on Associated Ethyl's 1939 shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Yost thanks the company for its shipment figures, assumes the material left the U.S., and notes notification and monthly reporting arrangements.

subfiles.title: Frank Howard report on proposed Manchukuo ethyl plant
subfiles.about: Seeks approval for handling Associated Ethyl negotiations over a proposed plant in Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Howard reports Associated Ethyl is discussing a Manchukuo ethyl plant but won't finalize anything while American shareholders regard the moral embargo as applicable.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Manchukuo plant negotiations
subfiles.about: Approves Howard's cautious approach as consistent with the moral-embargo policy.
subfiles.summary: Yost appreciates Howard's efforts to extend the December 20 policy and finds the procedure consistent with it, presuming British policy is similar.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese protest against aircraft moral embargo
subfiles.about: References a Japanese protest that the American aircraft moral embargo violated the 1911 treaty.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: the Japanese Embassy protests that State's July 1, 1938 circular to aircraft makers derogates from the 1911 treaty.

subfiles.title: Consular despatch on lead loaded aboard Akagi Maru
subfiles.about: Investigates Mexican lead loaded aboard the Japanese vessel Akagi Maru at Brownsville.
subfiles.summary: Consul reports 2,000 tons of ASARCO lead loaded at Brownsville, reviews Monterrey refineries and recent Mexican lead going to Japan, and says the nearby scrap's origin is unknown.

subfiles.title: A. Frasse inquiry about aircraft-alloy exports
subfiles.from: J. E. Lennon, A. Frasse & Co.
subfiles.about: Requests guidance on selling aircraft-grade alloy sheets and tubing through Volkart Brothers for Japan.
subfiles.summary: A. Frasse encloses Volkart Brothers' solicitation for aircraft-part alloys and asks whether accepting such business fits State's policies.

subfiles.title: Volkart Brothers proposal for Japanese alloy sales
subfiles.about: Proposes marketing chromium-molybdenum and chromium-nickel-molybdenum products in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Volkart says its Japanese affiliate wants alloy sheets and tubing for the aircraft industry and offers access to Japanese buyers, including government offices.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to A. Frasse
subfiles.about: Advises that the proposed aircraft-alloy export transaction would conflict with announced policy.
subfiles.summary: Department tells Frasse that sheets and tubing for Japan's aircraft industry would be inconsistent with the December 15 press release on aeronautical materials.

subfiles.title: Universal Oil Products appointment confirmation
subfiles.about: Confirms a meeting with Green at which Gustav Egloff will also be present.
subfiles.summary: Halle confirms an appointment for February 6, accompanied by Universal Oil Products research director Dr. Egloff.

subfiles.title: Shell Oil interim acknowledgment
subfiles.from: R. I. Lewis, Shell Oil Company
subfiles.about: Reports a delay in compiling requested shipment information.
subfiles.summary: Shell acknowledges the December 19 request and expects to complete the information early the following week.

subfiles.title: Shell Oil report on high-octane gasoline shipments
subfiles.about: Reports Shell's 1939 and early 1940 high-octane aviation-gasoline shipments to Japan and the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: Shell reports a 1939 shipment of 34,240 drums to Japan and a final 1940 consignment of 20,760 drums via Mitsui for the Japanese Navy, none to the Soviet Union, and promises future reports.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Shell aviation-gasoline report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Shell's report and promise to disclose future sales.
subfiles.summary: Department thanks Shell for its aviation-gasoline export information and notes its undertaking to report future transactions.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Congressman Celler about Japan Gasoline Company
subfiles.about: Records Celler's request for relief from the moral embargo's effect on a Japanese petroleum-technology contract.
subfiles.summary: Congressman Celler seeks a conference for ex-Congressman Cohen, whose Japan Gasoline Company interest suffered from suspension of a Universal Oil Products contract; Ballantine and Moseley will bring it to Green.

subfiles.title: Summary of Universal Oil Products contracts with Japan Gasoline Company
subfiles.about: Summarizes contracts, payments, plant orders, and arguments for exempting existing petroleum-technology work from the moral embargo.
subfiles.summary: Summary of Universal's contracts with Japan Gasoline Company, including a 1938 expansion paid $700,000, pending work for several Japanese firms, arguing they predate the embargo and Universal should complete them.

subfiles.title: Duplicate memorandum of conversation with Congressman Celler
subfiles.about: Duplicate record of Celler's intervention concerning the Universal Oil Products contract.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the account of Celler's appeal on behalf of former Congressman Cohen. It records discussion of a possible conference and Halle's forthcoming consultation with Green.

subfiles.title: Second duplicate memorandum of conversation with Congressman Celler
subfiles.about: A further copy of the memorandum concerning Celler and the suspended petroleum-technology contract.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum again describes Celler's concern over Cohen's investment and his request to convene the interested parties. Ballantine undertook to refer the matter to Green after Green's meeting with Halle.

subfiles.title: Green memorandum opposing an exception for Universal Oil Products
subfiles.about: Recommends denying any exception to the common suspension of aviation-gasoline technology contracts.
subfiles.summary: Green opposes an exception for Universal Oil Products, which joined the December 14 agreement to suspend contracts, since it would undermine equal treatment of cooperating firms.

subfiles.title: Green memorandum on calls with Celler and Halle
subfiles.about: Records telephone conversations confirming that no exception would be granted and that Universal intended to comply.
subfiles.summary: Green told Celler every participating company agreed to stop providing aviation-gasoline information; Halle says Celler, Cohen and three Japanese pressed him for an exception, which he refused.

subfiles.title: Chongqing Embassy despatch on proposed embargo petition
subfiles.from: Willys R. Peck, American Embassy, Chongqing
subfiles.about: Explains the Embassy's refusal to transmit a public petition demanding an embargo on munitions exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Peck encloses an American petition in Chongqing accusing the U.S. of participating in Japanese aggression, arguing it omits U.S. opposition and could inflame anti-American feeling, and asks approval of the Embassy's refusal to associate.

subfiles.title: McCurdy request to cable the Chongqing petition
subfiles.about: Requests that the Embassy cable an embargo petition signed by American residents to Washington.
subfiles.summary: McCurdy says about twenty-five American citizens in Chongqing support the petition and asks the Embassy to forward it so it can be released to local newspapers.

subfiles.title: Petition by American citizens in Chongqing
subfiles.to: President, Congress, and people of the United States
subfiles.about: Demands an immediate end to transactions supplying Japan's war effort.
subfiles.summary: Petition by Americans in Chongqing saying the U.S. facilitated Japanese aggression by supplying war materials, and appealing for immediate action now the commercial treaty has ended.

subfiles.title: List of attendees at the Chongqing International Club meeting
subfiles.about: Lists foreign and Chinese attendees associated with the meeting that produced the embargo appeal.
subfiles.summary: List of missionaries, teachers, journalists, bankers and others, with Chinese participants, attending the Chongqing International Club meeting.

subfiles.title: Embassy reply declining to transmit McCurdy's petition
subfiles.about: Declines to transmit the petition because publication would imply official American association with a partial statement.
subfiles.summary: Peck declines to transmit McCurdy's petition because it covers only one aspect of U.S. policy and might harm Sino-American friendship.

subfiles.title: Congressman Hall forwards constituent petition
subfiles.about: Forwards a petition from constituents concerned about war-material shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Congressman Hall sends Hull a constituent petition and says he told each constituent their concerns would be forwarded.

subfiles.title: Hull acknowledgment to Congressman Hall
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the petition opposing war-material shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull confirms receipt of Hall's letter and its enclosed petition. He thanks Hall for forwarding the communication.

subfiles.title: Christopher Graham letter enclosing a contribution
subfiles.about: Encloses a fifty-dollar check connected with opposition to Japanese aggression in China.
subfiles.summary: Christopher Graham sends a fifty-dollar check for the American Committee for Non-Participation in Japanese Aggression, not wishing to embarrass the President.

subfiles.title: Return of Christopher Graham's check
subfiles.about: Returns Graham's check because the Department does not act as a transmitting agency for private donations.
subfiles.summary: Yost returns Graham's check, explaining he can send it to the Committee directly and federal law doesn't restrict such contributions.

subfiles.title: Methodist petition for an embargo on war materials to Japan
subfiles.from: Members and friends of Methodist churches in the Portlandville–Oneonta area
subfiles.about: Condemns Japanese atrocities in China and urges legislation stopping American war-material exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Methodist petition describes Japanese bombing and the Nanjing atrocities, argues U.S. exports made America partly responsible, and calls for legislation ending basic war-material shipments.

subfiles.title: Japanese Chamber of Commerce request for export-control list
subfiles.from: Tatsuo Ono, Japanese Chamber of Commerce of New York
subfiles.about: Requests a complete list of commodities restricted or discouraged for sale or export to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Chamber of Commerce asks which goods fall under the moral embargo or resource-conservation controls.

subfiles.title: Reply to Japanese Chamber of Commerce
subfiles.to: Japanese Chamber of Commerce of New York
subfiles.about: Supplies policy documents on aeronautical goods and strategic materials.
subfiles.summary: Yost sends press releases and Munitions Board statements, explaining the measures apply to countries bombing civilians or to designated strategic materials.

subfiles.title: Justice Department referral of Henry Stimson correspondence
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of Henry L. Stimson's letter and enclosure on American Far Eastern policy.
subfiles.summary: Rogge sends State a photostat of Stimson's January 25 letter and enclosure, noting Stimson was informed.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Hamilton Fish on Japanese high-octane gasoline production
subfiles.about: Records Fish's request for authoritative information on Japan's ability to manufacture high-octane gasoline.
subfiles.summary: Fish says he has debated Upton Close over whether Japan possesses suitable factories and refineries. Hamilton replies that Japan buys substantial American supplies but that the more important question concerns access to technical production processes. He promises further inquiry through available diplomatic and commercial channels.

subfiles.title: Yost memorandum on Japanese aviation-gasoline capacity
subfiles.about: Summarizes limited intelligence on Japan's ability to produce aviation-gasoline blending agents.
subfiles.summary: Yost: Japan has few plants making blending agents, cannot meet more than a fraction of its aviation requirements, and its outdated processes can't produce top grades.

subfiles.title: Follow-up conversation with Hamilton Fish
subfiles.about: Provides Fish with production intelligence and American export figures for aviation gasoline.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine tells Hamilton Fish Japan's plants are few and outdated; 1939 U.S. exports were 513,411 barrels to Japan; Fish notes Japan might expand or get processes from Germany or Russia.

subfiles.title: Confidential instruction to the American Ambassador in Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits memoranda of the Hamilton Fish conversations for confidential information.
subfiles.summary: Instruction to Tokyo enclosing the January 11 and 15 conversations with Hamilton Fish on whether Japan makes high-octane gasoline.

subfiles.title: Triplicate memorandum on Senator Byrnes's export-statistics request
subfiles.to: Charles W. Yost and Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Records Byrnes's request for figures on war-material exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Senator Byrnes seeks six months of war-material export figures to Japan; Peurifoy says only figures for arms and implements of war under the May 1, 1937 proclamation exist, and will send the latest press release.

subfiles.title: Camden Forge inquiry about turbine and pinion shafts
subfiles.about: Requests guidance before accepting a Japanese order for nickel-chrome-molybdenum steel shafts.
subfiles.summary: Camden Forge asks whether a future embargo might cover turbine and pinion shafts for Japan and whether pre-embargo contracts could still be shipped.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Camden Forge
subfiles.about: Explains the absence of current statutory authority for a general Japan embargo and supplies relevant policy statements.
subfiles.summary: Yost states that no existing statute authorizes a general embargo on exports to Japan and that new legislation would be necessary. He cannot predict congressional action. He encloses statements on strategic materials, aeronautical equipment, and materials essential to airplane manufacture.

subfiles.title: Green memorandum on Braden Copper molybdenum sale
subfiles.about: Records Kennecott representatives' explanation of a proposed Chilean molybdenum sale to Japanese interests.
subfiles.summary: Braden Copper, Kennecott's Chilean subsidiary, has a Japanese order for seventy-five tons of molybdenum and fears refusal could provoke Chilean control; Green notes Chilean shipments fall outside U.S. policy.

subfiles.title: Duplicate memorandum on Braden Copper molybdenum sale
subfiles.about: Duplicate record of the proposed sale of Chilean molybdenum to Japanese buyers.
subfiles.summary: The duplicate repeats Kennecott's argument that Braden Copper should accept the seventy-five-ton order to avoid Chilean governmental intervention. It also repeats the production estimate of seventy to ninety tons monthly and the comparison with Japan's larger purchases from the United States.

subfiles.title: Inland Steel telegram on proposed Japanese sale
subfiles.from: J. L. Block, Inland Steel Company
subfiles.about: Requests immediate guidance on negotiations to sell up to 100,000 tons of semifinished steel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Inland Steel's Block reports talks on fifty to one hundred thousand tons of semifinished steel for Japan, asking State's wishes and a same-day reply.

subfiles.title: State Department letter to J. L. Block
subfiles.about: Follows the Department's telegram with policy statements relevant to the proposed steel sale.
subfiles.summary: State sends Block the December 15 and 20 statements on aeronautical materials for countries whose forces bomb civilians.
